intro: Owner direction (2026-09-11): remove the Future-scope toggle, give every top icon a border and a word, indent the accordion bodies, re-audit, and build the research features 01 02 04 07 10 11.

The Future-scope switch is gone and the four features it gated are simply the product now. Every top-bar and builder-header icon is a bordered button with a label. Section bodies are indented 44 px to the title.

Each feature below follows its design-office verdict (references/research/NN-*/05-directions.html). Prototype links open at the start of the journey (?focus=<id>). Copy is proposed, not approved — the sign-off list is under each feature.

The NG token pass (Phase 1 of the revamp) is still ahead: these screens carry the Studio X look. One token was fixed on the way: --muted-foreground now clears AA, which removed most of the Phase-0 axe nodes.

Second pass, same evening: seven owner notes on the first delivery — strip removed, ghost More, NG-style header controls, a better test rail, Figma overlaps fixed, contrast, and a where-it-lives table (below) — plus three follow-ups from screenshots: one header line, side-by-side architecture cards, one primary CTA per fold.

Third and fourth pass (2026-09-12): ten owner notes on the chrome (Run test scenarios as a header door, full-height rail, Undo to live, Callers hear as a field, hosting region as label + value, red End test, no em dashes anywhere in copy) and three on the models fold (voice selection in the TTS config, + Add backup beside every vendor, credentials as a switch modelled on the NG console). Then a presence check of all six features on production: every marker matched.

features.name: Top bar · builder header · accordion
features.jtbd: A first-time user can tell what every control at the top does, and nothing in the product bar is a demo device.

after.caption: After — live build

marks.why: Help · Notifications · Composer read as buttons; the Future-scope demo switch is gone — the roadmap features are the product now.

marks.name: Voice call, Custom config, More
marks.why: Every builder-header icon carries a border and a word; a first-time user can tell what each opens.

marks.name: Section body indented 44 px
marks.why: Controls align with the section title after the chevron, so each accordion reads as nested content.

marks.why: Help · Notifications · Composer are the NG console's 28 px icon controls: faint border, tint, the word in the tooltip and the accessible name; the bell wears the real unread count.

marks.name: More is a ghost button
marks.why: The overflow menu no longer competes with Voice call and Custom config, which keep their borders because they act.

after.caption: After (second pass) — the test rail: Scenarios (with count) · Voice call

marks.name: Scenarios · Voice call
marks.why: The rail's two tests are named by what you do — the generated suite with its count, or a live call. The active tab is a card with a 3:1 ring and semibold text, not a lighter shade of grey and not a CTA.

marks.name: One verb per tab
marks.why: Scenarios are generated, then run; the Voice call tab links back with “run the scenarios”, so neither tab is a dead end.

after.caption: After (second pass) — Who speaks first: the selected segment is unmistakable

marks.name: Selected segment is unmistakable
marks.why: Who speaks first — Agent / Caller: the chosen option is an ink-tinted chip with an ink border and semibold text; the other is outlined on border-stroke (≥ 3:1). The same rule now applies to every toggle group and tab in Studio X.

after.caption: After (second pass) — the same selected state on the call sheet's tabs

marks.name: Same selected state, app-wide
marks.why: The call sheet's tabs use the same card-with-ring selected state; the count badges stay readable and nothing reads as a primary button.

after.caption: After (third pass) — one header line across the rail, the section and the test rail

marks.name: One header line, three columns
marks.why: The rail header (n of 5 done · Collapse all), the section header and the test rail header are all 56 px with the same hairline, so the rule reads as one continuous line.

marks.name: Test rail header, same height
marks.why: Its bottom border now meets the section header's — the step that looked odd is gone.

after.caption: After (third pass) — Model Architecture cards side by side

marks.name: Cascading · Multimodal, left to right
marks.why: The two architecture cards sit side by side — one glance compares them; the stacked version read as a list.

after.caption: After (third pass, dark) — one primary CTA per fold; selected states are chips, not buttons

marks.name: Selected is a chip, not a CTA
marks.why: The active tab is a card with a 3:1 ring and semibold text — it no longer borrows the primary fill, so it stops competing with Deploy.

marks.name: One primary per fold
marks.why: Generate scenarios and Add case are outline buttons; Deploy in the header is the only filled CTA on screen.

after.caption: After (third pass): Run test scenarios is a header door; the rail runs the full viewport height

marks.name: Run test scenarios is a header door
marks.why: The scenario suite left the rail's tab strip; it opens the rail in its own mode next to Voice call and Custom config, and the open door reads as pressed.

marks.name: Rail runs the full viewport height
marks.why: The panel is the viewport height, so its left border reaches the bottom instead of stopping where the content ends.

after.caption: After (third pass): Callers hear is a read-only field with Hear the opening on the same line; no em dashes in copy

marks.name: Callers hear is a field, Hear the opening on the same line
marks.why: A read-only field like Greeting shows the exact composed line; the play button sits beside it. No new behaviour, the disclosure and greeting still compose it.

marks.name: No em dashes in copy
marks.why: Every em dash in user-facing text was rewritten: label pairs use a middot, sentences a period or colon. The failure, judge and hosting hints now read as sentences.

after.caption: After (third pass): Hosting region is label + value; what pinning changes lives in the info disclosure

marks.name: Region is label + value
marks.why: The options carry their name only; what pinning changes lives in the info disclosure, and a one-line consequence appears only when a region is pinned.

after.caption: After (third pass): End test uses the destructive variant

marks.name: End test is semantic red
marks.why: Ending a call, deleting, removing: the destructive variant (a tint of red) marks every action that stops or takes something away.

rationale: A switch that reveals unbuilt features in the product bar confuses reviewers (Phase 0 finding N4); now that the roadmap features are being built, they are shown.
Icon-only ghosts fail recognition over recall on a header with eight controls (A7); border + word costs 60 px and removes the guesswork.
44 px = padding + chevron + gap, so the body aligns with the title text — nested by geometry, not by a box.

Second pass (owner feedback, 2026-09-11 evening): the Start · Builder · All agents strip is gone (the breadcrumb carries location); More is a ghost button; Help · Notifications · Composer follow the NG console shell — 28 px ghost icon controls with a faint border and tint, the word in the tooltip and the accessible name, the real unread count on the bell.

Selected states: every toggle group and tab shares one rule — the chosen option is an ink-tinted chip with an ink border and semibold text (toggles) or a card with a 3:1 ring (tabs); the unchosen one is outlined on border-stroke. A first version used the primary fill and read as a CTA in dark mode, so it was replaced.
One primary per fold: Deploy owns the filled button; Generate scenarios and Add case in the test rail are outline.
The test rail's two tests are named by what you do — Scenarios (with its count) and Voice call — with a cross-link from the call to the scenarios; section 4 and the preflight say scenarios too.
The three builder columns share one 56 px header line (rail: n of 5 done · Collapse all; section header; test rail header). Model Architecture cards sit side by side.

Third pass (owner notes, 2026-09-12): the scenario suite left the rail's tab strip and became a header door, Run test scenarios, beside Custom config and Voice call; the open door reads as pressed. The rail is the viewport height so its border reaches the bottom. Reset to live is now Undo to live. Callers hear is a read-only field like Greeting, with Hear the opening on the same line and no new behaviour. Hosting region options carry their name only. End test, Delete and Remove use the destructive variant (a tint of red).

Copy rule, standing: no em dash in user-facing text. Every one was rewritten: label pairs use a middot, sentence elaborations a period or colon. The failure, judge and hosting hints now read as sentences.

marks.name: 01 · Voice picker
marks.why: Agent builder › Voice & Models › Select voice dialog: Recommended strip, Compare, Add your own voice.

rationale: The catalog has no use-case field; the agent's prompt is the use case — reading it costs nothing and needs no API.
Three recommended + three to compare is the Hick's-law budget.

Browse voices is a labelled button beside the field, not an icon; the pick updates vendor and voice together.

features.name: Greeting, filler & disclaimer
features.jtbd: The first seconds and the pauses feel natural — and compliant.
features.verdict: A as the spine, B's editable default, D as a recap line, E as the one button; C ships on Advanced.

before.caption: Before — a bare Greeting Message textarea

after.caption: After — Opening section on Prompt & knowledge, live build

marks.name: Opening
marks.why: Who speaks first · greeting · can callers interrupt it · tell the caller it's an AI · the exact line callers hear · silence recap · Hear the opening — one place for the first five seconds.

after.caption: Live check (2026-09-12, deploy mp4vnlddw): 04 on production

marks.name: 04 · Opening
marks.why: Agent builder › Prompt & knowledge: who speaks first, greeting, interrupt, AI disclosure, Callers hear, silence recap.

rationale: Article 50 has applied since 2 Aug 2026 — disclosure is the default where the greeting is authored, not an Advanced afterthought. New agents open with it on; existing greetings are never rewritten.
The prefix on the greeting is the only real write; showing the composed line keeps the hack honest.
Ported from the ng-console prototype (design/sandbox c4bba4e5) so both consoles carry the same grammar.

features.name: Vendors & provider fallback
features.jtbd: When a vendor is slow, down or blocked in my region, my live agents keep talking without me being paged.
features.verdict: A is the surface (one row, on by default), B is the fold (ordered pool with eligibility), C is one button (Test failover).

before.caption: Before — model stack with no fallback concept

after.caption: After — Backup providers row, live build

marks.name: Backup providers
marks.why: On by default; primary → backup per component in one recap; Change backups opens the ordered pool with eligibility; Test failover names the Engine dependency instead of pretending.

after.caption: After (fourth pass): + Add backup beside each vendor field; the ASR one opened into a Backup vendor select

marks.name: + Add backup beside each vendor
marks.why: A Backup vendor select appears under the field; the primary vendor is listed but disabled, ineligible vendors say why. The pick is the same one the Backup providers row recaps.

marks.name: One door per vendor
marks.why: LLM and TTS get the same ghost button; nothing is set until you pick.

after.caption: Live check (2026-09-12, deploy mp4vnlddw): 07 on production

marks.name: 07 · Backup providers
marks.why: Agent builder › Voice & Models, under the model stack: primary → backup per component, status chip, Change backups.

rationale: Managed is cheaper than BYO and includes vendor usage, so Agora can own the backup pool for managed components; a BYO component asks for a second key.
Pinning a hosting region costs failover — 'no eligible backup in Europe' is a real state with two real fixes (unpin, add a key).
The public agent API has no fallback field (Engine P1 · Nov): the pool is a draft field, the button says so.

Fourth pass (owner, 2026-09-12): + Add backup sits beside each vendor field in Configure models manually. It opens a Backup vendor select with the primary vendor listed but disabled and ineligible vendors saying why; the pick writes the same draft the Backup providers row recaps, so there is one truth.

Credentials are a switch modelled on the NG console's credential select (src/components/console/studio-resource-select.tsx): off is Agora Managed Key with the shield and Included, no key to add; on is a select of saved credentials with No credential selected and Create credential. A BYO-only vendor keeps the switch on and disabled. The earlier saved-credential placeholder name was wrong and is gone.
Same-day fix (bfb4406): the inline component existed but was never mounted in the slot rows, so the first production check found no + Add backup. The shots above are from the fixed deploy.
